As you can see at the bottom of the spine, this is Pocket Books #10, the last entry in the initial run of Pocket Books. This third printing is probably worth between \$15-25.

The most remarkable books in the haul are a few paperbacks from LA-based publisher Holloway House:

::: {.image-gallery-embed attrs="{\"gallery\":{\"images\":[{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/6a16f0f3-e87c-45d3-a926-0991bb7ec343_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/bfb94c6c-8b7d-4191-be94-7367eb7025e6_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/7192050f-4cd2-4c2d-8ee8-6183643d95a2_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/7bc10d5b-4cc4-48e5-a4e4-4ad6b38b6bc5_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/67126745-1e59-4d91-9ae6-32bad69fba9d_3072x4080.jpeg\"}],\"caption\":\"Holloway House paperbacks\",\"alt\":\"Coal, Street games, Radcliff #2: San Francisco Vendetta, Walking Black and Tall, and Long White Con\",\"staticGalleryImage\":{\"type\":\"image/png\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/0d3d5349-9ea8-46e7-b138-0dc12e21edb6_1456x1210.png\"}},\"isEditorNode\":true}"}
:::

The subject matter of these books are evocative of the [Blaxploitation film movement](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Blaxploitation), but I couldn't think of a literary genre to give them. Kinohi Nishikawa assigns them the category "Black pulp fiction" in his book about Holloway House, *Street Players,* [reviewed here by the AAIHS](https://www.aaihs.org/holloway-house-and-the-black-literary-underground/). Apart from Nishikawa's book, there seems little written about this house or its authors. Some of these books are so obscure I had trouble verifying their editions. For instance, it seems there is no copy of *Walking Black and Tall* currently for sale on the internet. I look forward to reading *Street Players*, as it argues that, just as the best Blaxploitation films did, Holloway House's books embraced, but also transcended, the market demand for sensationalist content and evolved into what he called a "Black literary underground." The book *Death for Hire* by Joseph Nazel serves as an excellent illustration:

::: {.image-gallery-embed attrs="{\"gallery\":{\"images\":[{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/c4e34f67-8af5-4b1d-b1fa-e1f79ebefcb8_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/8edd6409-11e3-420d-b2ef-b9a4af29bd24_3072x4080.jpeg\"},{\"type\":\"image/jpeg\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/1fbea959-6768-4a46-bc33-677f96dde833_3072x4080.jpeg\"}],\"caption\":\"Death for Hire by Joseph Nazel\",\"alt\":\"The front cover, back cover, and dedication of Death for Hire\",\"staticGalleryImage\":{\"type\":\"image/png\",\"src\":\"https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/f6d3537a-bb34-44e8-878a-ec67c1cc7165_1456x474.png\"}},\"isEditorNode\":true}"}
:::

The back describes the premise:

> Sugar Man's a high-powered underworld king who specializes in supplying the poison that the frustrated and needy pump into their veins. But the Assistant D.A.'s hot on his tail, willing and ready to put him and all the other dope dealers away. Sugar Man doesn't to make the hit, not when the courts are so lenient with juveniles. They can beat raps that adults can't! So he recruits two teenagers, Trace and Turtle, who idolize the underworld king and who cheerfully waste the prosecutor. Unfortunately the bloody scene panics Tracy, who slams into a police car while trying to escape. Then the luckless young-blood has Sugar Man on his tail, as well as the black and white predators of the inner city jungle! Should juveniles be handled with the same laws and punishment that govern adults? This gripping book lays bare the consequences.

Superficially it resembles closely the premises of other pearl-clutching exploitation works about urban crime from the 50s onward, but Nazel reveals his literary aspirations with the dedication:

> Dedication:
>
> To James Baldwin, Langston Hughes, Richard Wright and the other brilliant brothers who have painted the Black experience for us over the years.
>
> J.N.

I'll be keeping *Death for Hire* to read, but the others will be for sale on my eBay store soon, or on my Whatnot shows. As always, make me an offer here or on Instagram if you'd like to buy any of the books in my haul before they're listed publicly.
